fields.v: Ding, J., Long, S., Pu, C., Zhang, G., Zhou, H. (leading authors), et al.; corresponding Chen, X., Huang, W., Zhang, G. (2025). NL2Repo-Bench: Towards Long-Horizon Repository Generation Evaluation of Coding Agents. arXiv:2512.12730v2 [cs.CL], 8 Jan 2026
2025 (arXiv v1 2025; v2 dated 8 Jan 2026)
Preprint — arXiv:2512.12730v2 [cs.CL]

Industry and academia: ByteDance Seed China (corresponding authors), M-A-P, 2077AI, Humanlaya Data, Nanjing University, Peking University, Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Beihang University

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — NL2Repo-Bench benchmark (104 tasks: build a complete installable Python library from a single natural-language requirements document in an empty workspace, scored by the upstream pytest suite); baseline results for 10 models in OpenHands-CodeAct plus Claude Code and Cursor-CLI, with failure analysis and two ablations

Coding agents/frameworks compared: OpenHands-CodeAct agent (main framework), Claude Code, Cursor-CLI; no versions. Models: DeepSeek-V3.1, DeepSeek-V3.2, Qwen3-235B-Instruct, Qwen3-235B-Thinking, Kimi-k2, GLM-4.6, Claude-Sonnet-4, Claude-Sonnet-4.5, Gemini-3-pro (via Cursor-CLI), GPT-5. No SDD approach

Benchmark input (not an approach): one natural-language specification document per task with four sections: Project Description; Supports (third-party packages with versions, expected directory structure); API Usage Guide (classes, functions, signatures, expected behaviour, import instructions); Implementation Nodes (concrete examples for critical APIs). Average ~18,800 tokens. Written by annotators by reverse-engineering the upstream repository (AST-assisted, AI drafting allowed, manually verified)

No prescribed flow: agent gets an empty workspace with the spec document and a single initialization instruction, then works autonomously (free choice of tools, unlimited rounds); workspace is then packaged and the upstream pytest suite run in a Docker testing image. Benchmark construction: repository selection -> environment/test validation -> spec writing -> human expert review, static AST coverage check, preliminary agent runs with failure analysis by a senior engineer -> refinement
None during agent runs (fully autonomous after one instruction). Human review only in benchmark construction (Python experts verify spec fidelity; senior engineer analyses failing tests)
Full agent run from specification to repository (the specification is the benchmark input, not an SDD workflow)
Not classifiable (benchmark of coding agents; the input is a detailed natural-language 'specification' document, but no SDD approach; authors do not use SDD terms)
New project: generate a complete installable Python library from scratch (empty workspace) reproducing a real open-source repository

104 tasks; source repositories 300-120,000 LOC at selection; difficulty Easy <=1,500 LOC (26), Medium 1,500-4,000 LOC (46), Hard >=4,000 LOC (32); spec ~18,800 tokens on average; ~180 interaction turns on average for Claude-Sonnet-4.5

Python libraries in 9 categories: Web Development 10, Testing 13, Utility Libraries 11, Machine Learning 7, Data Analysis & Processing 18, Database Interaction 7, Networking Tools 9, Batch File Processing 5, System Tools 24
N/A (no human participants in the runs; annotators, Python experts and a senior Python engineer build the benchmark)

No token, time or money metrics. Effort proxies: interaction turns per task (avg, std, max; turns/score ratio, Table 6); total tool invocations and per task (Table 7, Fig. 7 axis labelled 'Cost/Effort')
Average test pass rate on the upstream pytest suite (task score; overall, by difficulty and by category); Pass@1 count = number of tasks whose full test suite passes in a single run
None
None

Early-termination rate (finish invoked within <100 turns) and non-finish rate (finish never invoked); tool-call distribution and correlation of tool usage with score (Table 5); tool-transition workflow patterns (edit-test loop, navigation trap, blind editing); failure taxonomy (ImportError/ModuleNotFound, test-suite alignment); performance by context-window size

Automatic: generated workspace run against the original pytest suite in a per-task Docker image (modified so collection errors do not abort the run); tool calls and turns from agent traces. Manual/qualitative: case analyses of failures and workflow patterns

Benchmark NL2Repo-Bench, 104 tasks, one run each. Criterion: average pass rate on upstream tests and Pass@1 count; no success criterion stated by the authors. Overall % (Pass@1) [avg turns; tool calls per task, Tables 6-7, OpenHands only]: (1) Claude Code + Claude-Sonnet-4.5: 40.2 (3); (2) OpenHands + Claude-Sonnet-4.5: 39.9 (3) [181.6; 85.98]; (3) Cursor-CLI + Claude-Sonnet-4.5: 39.2 (4); (4) OpenHands + Claude-Sonnet-4: 37.0 (5) [180.7; 85.38]; (5) Cursor-CLI + Gemini-3-pro: 34.2 (3); (6) OpenHands + DeepSeek-V3.2: 27.6 (1) [254.3; 120.59]; (7) OpenHands + Kimi-k2: 22.7 (3) [275.1; 126.42]; (8) OpenHands + DeepSeek-V3.1: 22.2 (1) [202.3; 94.88]; (9) OpenHands + GPT-5: 21.7 (1) [78.4; 34.30]; (10) OpenHands + Qwen3-Instruct: 17.9 (1) [212.9; 100.28]; (11) OpenHands + GLM-4.6: 17.5 (2) [138.6; 62.79]; (12) OpenHands + Qwen3-Thinking: 13.8 (1) [70.2; 30.13]. For each: quality verdict no criterion stated by the authors (authors call long-horizon repository generation 'largely unsolved'); cost verdict no criterion stated by the authors (no tokens, time or money; only turns and tool calls as effort proxies, not reported for Claude Code and Cursor-CLI). Ablation (round limit 50-500, Claude-Sonnet-4.5, framework not stated): score rises up to 200 rounds then saturates (values only in Fig. 9); no criterion stated. Ablation (Claude Code + Claude-Sonnet-4.5 with all tests visible): 59.4% (Pass@1 18) vs 40.2% (3); Easy 73.2 / Medium 67.5 / Hard 35.6; no criterion stated

Tasks: 104 NL2Repo tasks (spec document + empty workspace). Configurations: 10 models in OpenHands-CodeAct (Gemini-3-pro via Cursor-CLI because of agent-in-a-loop errors in OpenHands) plus Claude-Sonnet-4.5 in Claude Code and Cursor-CLI. Baseline: none (leaderboard). Held constant: task document, empty workspace, single initialization instruction, no human input, no round limit, same Docker evaluation image; model fixed (Claude-Sonnet-4.5) across three frameworks to isolate the framework. Acceptance tests: upstream repository pytest suites (hidden from the agent). Repetitions: single run (Pass@1). Human intervention: none after the initial instruction

Claude Code + Claude-Sonnet-4.5 best (40.2%), then OpenHands + Claude-Sonnet-4.5 39.9% and Cursor-CLI 39.2%; Qwen3-Thinking lowest (13.8%). Same model differs by <1% across the three frameworks, so model capability dominates ('model-centric benchmark'). Performance falls with difficulty (e.g. Claude Code 51.8 Easy / 44.5 Medium / 25.1 Hard). Long-context models lead; GPT-5 halts awaiting user input (non-finish 84.5%); Qwen3-Thinking early-terminates in 49.0%. task_tracker usage correlates 0.711 with score. Showing tests raises Claude Code to 59.4%. No significance tests

Distinguished models clearly (13.8-40.2%) and difficulty levels; did not distinguish frameworks with the same model (<1%), which the authors read as the benchmark being model-centric. Repeatability not assessed (single run, no variance reported). No limitations of the comparison method stated

No limitations or threats section. Gaps stated: long-horizon repository generation largely unsolved; progress needs agentic planning, self-verification/self-correction loops, global coherence mechanisms and reliable environment management beyond larger context windows; early termination of thinking models and 'collaborative bias' of GPT-5

Inconsistencies: abstract 'below 40%' and conclusion 'Claude-Sonnet-4.5 ... 39.6% pass rate' vs Table 3 40.2% (Claude Code) / 39.9% (OpenHands); text 'below 40.5%' (p. 9); text says the strongest model fully passes 'only five repositories' but Table 3 gives Pass@1 3 for the top configuration (5 is Claude-Sonnet-4); Table 6 gives DeepSeek-V3.2 a score of 22.2% (and turns/score 1145.5 computed from it) vs 27.6% in Table 3, Fig. 5 and the text; Fig. 6 N=8980 for Claude-Sonnet-4 vs Table 7 total 8880. Values from Table 3 used. Data: dataset, Docker environments and evaluation toolkit released (github.com/multimodal-art-projection/NL2RepoBench). No pre-registration. Programming language: Python

fields.why: Judgement call: negative results are reported openly, but the context-window and planning explanations rest on correlations without tests, and the headline figures in the abstract (below 40%) and conclusion (39.6%) differ from Table 3; another reader could give Yes
fields.doubt: Os resultados negativos estão relatados, mas as causas (janela de contexto, planeamento) assentam em correlações e o resumo/conclusão diferem da Tabela 3. Decide entre Partly e Yes.
